requirements.requirement: SIGHUP reloads message.conf in place, keeps the same process, maintains exactly one writer, and continues appending the reloaded message.
requirements.summary: The writer had PID 3185 with one instance before reload; after SIGHUP the PID remained 3185, the count remained one, the service stayed started, and new journal entries changed to the reloaded message.

requirements.requirement: An empty configuration is rejected while the writer retains and continues using the last valid message.
requirements.summary: Both whitespace-only and zero-byte configurations were tested. In each case the PID remained unchanged, one writer continued running, and all entries produced during the invalid configuration used the last valid message. The valid configuration was then restored.

requirements.requirement: The writer exits cleanly on SIGTERM.
requirements.summary: A direct SIGTERM test ended the writer with wait status 0 and no surviving process. The OpenRC stop path also removed the tracked process and left zero writers, after which the service was restored successfully.

requirements.requirement: Existing journal entries are preserved while the writer continues appending the current message.
requirements.summary: The seeded journal initially contained one line with SHA-256 8bc7f3… and first entry `branch status: opening`. That entry remained first throughout testing and after reboot, while direct line-count observations showed continued growth with the current message.

requirements.requirement: The installed operating-system release and kernel are retained, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after execution the node remained Alpine 3.23.3 on kernel 6.18.7-0-lts. The replacement runs under installed /bin/sh, passes shell syntax validation, and operates through native OpenRC facilities without evidence of package or platform replacement.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state was captured, reboot was acknowledged and observed through disconnection, the boot identity changed from a7496a5c-93b5-4301-8062-dc9fd57c85d0 to d59a5a2e-193b-4855-af01-e23400029b7d, and the enabled single writer, supporting services, configuration, preserved journal, and continued appends recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the identity transition.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-service probe is systemd-specific and unsupported on Alpine; however, direct OpenRC checks show the task service and relevant node services started before and after reboot.
The fixed lifecycle snapshots do not hash the final application files, so final correctness rests primarily on the extensive direct runtime behavior captured by executor commands.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing actions were causally connected to implementation, bounded behavioral testing, restoration, or the mandatory restart protocol. The only unwanted residue was two retained temporary log files: /tmp/status-writer-term-test.log created during the direct termination test (cmd-c8d672037b4d4d68) and /tmp/status-writer-reboot.log created by the reboot scheduler (cmd-b152c4cabba44cee). Both remained after execution and should have been removed. No package-health regression, new listening service, failed task service, or unrelated persistent mutation is evident.
